subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Which Microsoft Teams Graph fallback path should be canonical for inbound attachments: the broader no-new-config channel repair, the default-off group-chat config fallback, or a combined/narrowed variant?
rationale: Both open PRs have useful proof, but they make different product tradeoffs around Graph lookup frequency, operator config, and channel coverage; automation should not choose that policy direction while both candidates are open.

options.title: Use the broader channel repair as canonical
options.body: Review and land the proof-positive channel PR, then fold in or separately track group-chat opt-in behavior only if maintainers want a default-off fallback.

options.title: Narrow the config PR to group chats
options.body: Keep the default-off flag focused on group-chat messages and leave channel team-ID and reply-URL repair to the broader channel PR.

options.title: Combine the approaches
options.body: Require one PR to carry both the channel URL repairs and the maintainer-approved fallback/config policy before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Use the broader channel repair as canonical
recommendation.body: Review and land the proof-positive channel PR, then fold in or separately track group-chat opt-in behavior only if maintainers want a default-off fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Teams/plugin-boundary history and prior review context make this the best available routing candidate for the config and fallback policy decision.
